title: 1D Array Indexing (Positive & Negative)
description: Access individual elements in a 1D NumPy array using 0-based positive indexes and negative indexes counting from the end.
code:
import numpy as np

numbers = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50])

print("First element (index 0):", numbers[0])
print("Third element (index 2):", numbers[2])
print("Last element (index -1):", numbers[-1])
print("Second-last element (index -2):", numbers[-2])
expectedOutput:
First element (index 0): 10
Third element (index 2): 30
Last element (index -1): 50
Second-last element (index -2): 40
explanation: Indexing in Python starts at 0. Negative indexes start at -1 from the end of the array, so numbers[-1] gives 50 without needing the array length.

title: 1D Array Slicing (Ranges & Steps)
description: Extract sub-ranges of values using start:stop and start:stop:step syntax where start is included and stop is excluded.
code:
import numpy as np

numbers = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60])

print("Slice [1:4]:", numbers[1:4])
print("Slice [:3]:", numbers[:3])
print("Slice [2:]:", numbers[2:])
print("Slice [-3:]:", numbers[-3:])
print("Step slice [0:6:2]:", numbers[0:6:2])
explanation: In numbers[1:4], values at indices 1, 2, and 3 are returned. Stop index 4 is excluded. Omitting start defaults to index 0, and omitting stop defaults to the end.

title: 2D Row & Column Selection with Colon (:)
description: Select individual elements, complete rows, and complete columns from a 2D matrix.
code:
import numpy as np

marks = np.array([
    [80, 75, 90],
    [70, 85, 88],
    [92, 78, 95]
])

print("Specific element [1, 2]:", marks[1, 2])
print("Row 0 (First student):", marks[0])
print("Column 0 (Maths marks):", marks[:, 0])
print("Column 1 (English marks):", marks[:, 1])
expectedOutput:
Specific element [1, 2]: 88
Row 0 (First student): [80 75 90]
Column 0 (Maths marks): [80 70 92]
Column 1 (English marks): [75 85 78]
explanation: marks[row, col] accesses a single scalar. marks[0] selects the entire first row. marks[:, 0] uses the colon (:) to select all rows across column 0.

title: 2D Sub-Matrix Slicing & In-Place Updates
description: Extract rectangular sub-regions of a 2D array and perform in-place vector arithmetic.
code:
import numpy as np

marks = np.array([
    [80, 75, 90],
    [70, 85, 88],
    [92, 78, 95]
])

# Slicing rows 0:2 and columns 1:3
sub_grid = marks[0:2, 1:3]
print("Sub-grid [0:2, 1:3]:\n", sub_grid)

# Add 5 bonus marks to Maths (column 0) for first two students
marks[0:2, 0] = marks[0:2, 0] + 5
print("\nUpdated array after +5 bonus to Maths for first two students:\n", marks)
expectedOutput:
Sub-grid [0:2, 1:3]:
 [[75 90]
 [85 88]]

Updated array after +5 bonus to Maths for first two students:
 [[85 75 90]
 [75 85 88]
 [92 78 95]]
explanation: marks[0:2, 1:3] extracts a 2x2 rectangular sub-matrix. Assignment to slices allows fast in-place vector updates on targeted sub-regions.
